open_questions: Centroid is inconclusive (why: no sector with a clear difference image) - on-target location not directly verified
Star hosts very strong variability (amplitude ~15485 ppm, rotation period 7.369 d) which can affect depths for a 10.38 SNR, 3-transit signal
Only 3 transits with refit share 0.4362 and p_chance 0.007167 for gap pattern - more transits needed to confirm at 13.2 d
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a 1.5-hour, flat-bottomed dip repeating every 13.2 days on a nearby M dwarf, implying a 3.9-Earth-radius planet with no odd-even change or secondary eclipse and no nearby star that could mimic it. The dip shape, size and duration favour a small planet over a stellar eclipse. The star is very spotted and has only three observed transits, so additional follow-up will fully confirm the period and rule out blends.

reasons.why: Negatively V-shaped (flat-bottomed) transit, favouring a planet over a grazing/stellar eclipse.
Planet-sized (well below ~10 Rearth, host is a 0.2994 Rsun M dwarf from TIC).
Observed 1.499 h / central 1.971 h duration is near 1, consistent with central transit and low impact parameter fit_b 0.06948.
No odd/even depth difference (14560 vs 13880 ppm, diff_ratio 1).
No significant secondary eclipse (below 5 threshold, similar to best brightening 3.524, inconsistent with stellar companion).
No star within 21 arcsec can plausibly cause the dip with <25% eclipse; closest that could is 56.8 arcsec away needing 0.2182 eclipse.
No sector with a clear difference image but flat, non-V dip on target outweighs blending and cannot be placed on a neighbour given neighbour search.
